issues.legal_issue: A former minor’s suit to set aside a guardian’s transfer of immovable property and recover possession is governed by the limitation rule for setting aside a guardian’s transfer.
material_facts: The plaintiffs challenged transfers made by their mother, who was their natural guardian, of property in which they claimed shares.
The suit sought to set aside the transfers and recover possession.
The transfers were alleged to have been made without legal necessity and without the required court permission.
issues.conclusion: The suit was governed by Article 60 of the Limitation Act, 1963, rather than Articles 109, 110 or 113. A former minor challenging a transfer made by a guardian in contravention of Section 8 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, and seeking possession must sue within the period prescribed by Article 60 after attaining majority.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8(1) and 8(2)(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, govern the natural guardian’s authority to deal with a minor’s property and the required permission for a sale. A transfer in contravention of those requirements is voidable and must be set aside before possession can be recovered. Article 60 of the Limitation Act applies to a former minor’s suit to set aside a guardian’s transfer, including where possession is sought as consequential relief. Article 109 concerns a father’s alienation of ancestral property; Article 110 concerns enforcing a share after exclusion from joint-family property; Article 113 is residual and does not apply where Article 60 governs. No earlier cases are cited or relied on.

rule.if: suit_challenges_guardian_transfer and claimant_was_minor_when_transfer and transfer_breached_guardian_authority_requirements and relief_seeks_to_set_aside_transfer

predicates.suit_challenges_guardian_transfer: The proceeding is a suit challenging a transfer of property made by a guardian.
predicates.claimant_was_minor_when_transfer: The claimant whose property interest is challenged was a minor when the transfer occurred.
predicates.transfer_breached_guardian_authority_req: The guardian made the transfer without satisfying the requirements governing dealings with the minor’s property.
predicates.relief_seeks_to_set_aside_transfer: The claimant seeks to set aside the transfer, whether or not possession is also sought.

issues.definition: When a former minor sues to set aside a guardian’s transfer that breached the guardian’s authority, the suit falls under the rule for limitation of challenges to guardian transfers.

issues.legal_issue: Where several persons jointly entitled to sue challenge a guardian’s transfer, the limitation period is determined by applying the rule for multiple persons with a disability together with the former minor’s limitation rule.
material_facts: The suit was brought by several plaintiffs claiming interests in the same property, and one plaintiff was still a minor when it was filed.
The first plaintiff was 20 years old when the suit was filed, placing the filing within three years after he attained majority.
The other adult plaintiffs were not managers or the Karta of the joint family.
issues.conclusion: The suit was filed within limitation. The adult plaintiffs did not trigger the relevant rule as persons capable of giving a discharge without the concurrence of the others, and the first plaintiff filed within three years after attaining majority.
issues.legal_principle: Article 60 of the Limitation Act, 1963, allows a former minor to sue within three years after attaining majority to set aside a guardian’s transfer. Under Section 7, where several persons are jointly entitled to sue, time runs against all if a discharge can be given without the concurrence of the person under disability; otherwise, time does not run against them until a person becomes capable of giving such a discharge or the disability ceases. Explanation II to Section 7 treats a Mitakshara Hindu undivided family manager as capable of giving a discharge without concurrence only when that person is managing the joint-family property. No earlier cases are cited or relied on.

rule.if: suit_challenges_guardian_transfer and claimants_jointly_entitled_to_sue and one_claimant_was_minor and adult_claimants_not_joint_family_managers and filing_within_first_claimants_post_majority_period

predicates.suit_challenges_guardian_transfer: The proceeding is a suit challenging a transfer of property made by a guardian.
predicates.claimants_jointly_entitled_to_sue: Several claimants assert joint entitlement to bring the suit concerning the property.
predicates.one_claimant_was_minor: At least one claimant was a minor when the suit was filed.
predicates.adult_claimants_not_joint_family_manager: The adult claimants were not managing the joint-family property as its manager or Karta.
predicates.filing_within_first_claimants_post_major: The suit was filed within the applicable period after the first plaintiff attained majority.

issues.definition: When several persons jointly sue to challenge a guardian’s transfer, an underage claimant’s limitation position and the adult claimants’ lack of authority to give a discharge without concurrence may leave the suit timely if it was filed within the first plaintiff’s post-majority period.
